long_biography.plain_text:
Ratcliffe trained as a chemical engineer and completed an MBA at London Business School while working for Exxon Chemicals. He later moved to Courtaulds and into private equity, where he learned to structure industrial buyouts. In 1992 he led the acquisition that created Inspec, before leaving six years later to acquire an Antwerp chemicals operation and establish INEOS.

INEOS grew through tightly financed acquisitions of industrial assets, most dramatically the 2005 purchase of BP's Innovene business. That transaction propelled the group among the world's largest chemicals manufacturers. Ratcliffe remains its founder, chairman and majority owner. The group has expanded into oil and gas, automotive manufacturing and sports investments, but his fortune and operating identity remain rooted in industrial manufacturing.
